units.source_text: 源氏公子知道将来终有返京之一日。

en.t: Prince Genji knew that one day in the future he would surely return to the capital.

units.source_text: 然而人世无常，变化不测，结局如何，安能逆料？

en.t: Yet human life is uncertain, and its changes cannot be predicted; how could anyone know in advance how things would end?
Because of this, he often grieved and sighed.

units.source_text: 正在此时，突然接到了催促归京的圣旨。

en.t: Just then, an imperial order suddenly arrived urging him to return to the capital.

units.source_text: 他一方面欢庆喜慰，另一方面想起了今当告辞此浦，又不免惜别伤离。

en.t: On the one hand he rejoiced and felt relieved, but on the other, when he thought that he must now take leave of this shore, he could not help feeling the sorrow of parting.

units.source_text: 明石道人呢，明知源氏公子返京乃当然之事，然而闻此消息，立刻胸怀郁结，不胜悲伤。

en.t: As for the Akashi monk, although he knew perfectly well that Prince Genji's return to the capital was only natural, the moment he heard the news his heart grew heavy and he was overwhelmed with grief.

units.source_text: 既而转念一想：“只要公子青云得意，我便可如愿以偿。”

en.t: After a while he thought again, "As long as the prince rises to high fortune, my own wish will be fulfilled."
